result.title: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively
result.comment: 32 pages, 6 figures. Code and model are available at https://github.com/SALT-NLP/Sherpa
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly capable problem solvers, but being able to solve a problem is not the same as being able to teach it. Existing approaches to training LLMs as teachers rely on demonstrations, preference data, or predefined pedagogical criteria that specify what good teaching looks like. However, these signals are often not grounded in individual student learning outcomes, where effective teaching strategies can vary substantially across learners. To address this, we introduce Sherpa, a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that instantiates multiple student archetypes with LLMs conditioned on distinct learning preferences and trains a teacher model to adapt its instruction by directly maximizing their learning outcomes. Teacher LLMs trained with Sherpa improve instructed students' performance across all archetypes by an average of 20.5 percentage points. Under MathTutorBench's evaluation, Sherpa raises the overall pedagogy score from 52.5% to 79.2%, indicating better teaching responses. Our human studies show that the trained teacher is preferred over the base model in 79.6% of pairwise comparisons. Together, Sherpa trains LLM teachers to adapt to diverse simulated students and become better aligned with human teachers, paving the road towards AI tutors teaching real students.

AI.brief_summary: Sherpa 提出多轮强化学习框架，用不同学习偏好的学生原型模拟学习者，训练教师模型根据学习成效自适应调整教学策略，在模拟学生表现、教学评分与人工偏好上均有提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作是纯文本教学对话自适应，缺少视觉或多模态推理状态线索；不过其「按学习者状态调整指令、以结果反馈训练策略」的多轮 RL 设定，可能与 LVR 中按内部状态决定后续 LOOK/THINK/STOP 的自适应计算存在类比，相关程度需核查原文细节。
